newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse rebounds after intra-day correction.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse rebounds after intra-day correction.

text.p: Greek stocks ended 0.67 higher after an intra-day correction on Friday with market watchers saying buying interest continued to be strong.

"The market showed its momentum on Friday. It closed higher after an intra-day correction because of growing investment interest from all over Greece and foreign investors," said Dimitris Tamvakas, an analyst at Ionian Securities.

Long-term bourse prospects are good and Greece is among the top three emerging markets in terms of annual growth in weighted earnings per share which is estimated at around 15 percent for 1997, he said.
Greek equities were trading at a P/E of 10.2 on 1996 earnings and 8.5 in 1997 and this was clearly attractive.
However, a healthy correction after the bourse's recent sharp rise could occur in the following sessions and the general share index could eventually drop to 1,150 points, he said.
Tamvakas expects banks, large construction and cement firms to be this year's protagonists.
Construction shares were down approximately 20 percent compared to early 1995 prices according to a recent estimate and this means they have not recovered and have more to go on the upside.
The Athens general share index settled 0.67 percent or 8.24 points higher at 1238.44 points from Thursday's 1230.20, after opening at 1222.50.
Losers led gainers 124 to 97 with 27 issues unchanged on 248 traded. Turnover was 14.4 billion drachmas on volume of 4.2 million shares.
Banks rose 0.95 percent but construction lost 0.20 percent. Industrials gained 1.09 percent and leasing shares dropped 0.76 percent. Small-caps ended 1.33 percent weaker.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 962.00-980.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, lost 45 drachmas at 5,705.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $27.72-$28.97. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 9,604-10,189 drachmas.
